How i prepared for Leadership Questions (Behaviourval Questions) asked for Amazon.
During Amazon interview , you will come across question on Leadership Principles in each round and this is really important to get into Amazon.
So don't neglect this if you get chance to interview with Amazon.
HR had told me to answer all Leadership Questions (Behaviourval) using ‘STAR’ pattern.
S(Situation): Describe the SITUATION you were in.
T(task): Explain the TASK that needed to be done.
A(Action): Detail the ACTION that you took to achieve the task.
R(Result): Reveal the RESULTS of your action.
How to answer in better way:
1) Give all answer using STAR pattern.
2) Give answer relating to your work experience / projects using technical terms to get good impression rather than giving general answer.
Note: I gave very generalised answer in 1st round and feedback was mixed for behavioural question.
What all questions i have prepared?
-> I just researched for few hours and went through a more than 20+ recent interview experiences on Leetcode and noted all unique Leadership questions(behavioural) at once place.
-> Prepared for each question using STAR pattern relating to my experience with different different technical terms.
-> For 1-2 questions that i was not able to relate to my experiences in better way, i took help of chatgpt to frame a better answer.
Note: I encountered most of the exact questions that I had researched and collected. I am sharing a Google Doc link where I noted these questions with two youtube video link inside this.
Google Doc link: https://lnkd.in/gJtmF7YP
Note: I really liked this “STAR’ technique and we can use in other companies as well to answer behavioral questions.
Before my Amazon interview, I used to be very scared of behavioral questions. However, after the interview, I am no longer afraid of them and feel much more confident.
Keep coding, Keep applying!!

ai_analysis.summary: This is a personal account of preparing for Amazon behavioral and leadership interviews. It emphasizes that Leadership Principle questions can appear in each round and recommends using the STAR pattern: Situation, Task, Action, and Result. The author advises grounding answers in previous work and projects and using relevant technical terms rather than giving general responses. The preparation involved reviewing more than 20 recent interview experiences on LeetCode, collecting recurring leadership questions, and preparing STAR-based answers. The supplied content does not list the actual leadership questions.

interview_questions.question: What is the STAR pattern, and what does each component require?
interview_questions.answer:
Situation describes the context in which the candidate was operating.
Task explains the objective that needed to be accomplished.
Action details what the candidate did to achieve the task.
Result explains what the candidate's action produced.

interview_questions.question: How should a candidate prepare to answer Amazon leadership and behavioral questions?
interview_questions.answer:
The candidate should recognize that leadership questions may appear in each round.
The candidate should prepare answers using the STAR pattern.
The candidate should connect answers to real work experience and projects.
The candidate should use relevant technical terms rather than giving only a general response.

interview_questions.question: A candidate receives mixed feedback after giving a generalized behavioral answer in an interview. How should the candidate adjust?
interview_questions.answer:
The candidate should replace the generalized response with an answer grounded in relevant work experience or projects.
The candidate should organize the response with Situation, Task, Action, and Result.
The candidate should incorporate appropriate technical terms from personal experience.

interview_questions.question: How can someone prepare a bank of likely behavioral questions before an Amazon interview?
interview_questions.answer:
The person can review recent interview experiences, such as those found on LeetCode.
The person can collect recurring or unique leadership questions in one place.
The person can prepare a STAR-based answer for each question and tailor it to personal experience.
The post describes using ChatGPT to frame answers for one or two questions that could not be connected well to the candidate's experience.
